draft.title: Physiological adaptations to training
card: An adaptation is a lasting change the body makes in response to regular training. It builds up over weeks and months, and it fades if training stops.
Stroke volume is the amount of blood the heart pumps out in one beat. Training strengthens the heart, so stroke volume rises, including at rest.
Cardiac output is heart rate × stroke volume. At rest the body needs about the same blood flow, so a larger stroke volume means the heart beats less often. Resting heart rate falls.
VO₂ max is the most oxygen the body can take in and use in a minute. It rises with aerobic training. Muscles also grow bigger (hypertrophy) and get better at using oxygen to make energy.
draft.remember: Training makes the heart pump more per beat, so it beats less often at rest, and muscles use oxygen better.

a.q: After months of training, Leila's resting heart rate drops from 72 to 60 beats per minute. What best explains this change?
opts: Her heart pumps more blood with each beat
Her heart is pumping less blood each minute
Her muscles have lost their ability to use oxygen
Her VO₂ max has fallen as her heart has rested
a.why: A stronger heart has a higher stroke volume, so it can supply the same blood flow with fewer beats. The second option is tempting, but the body still needs about the same blood flow at rest, so the heart does not pump less each minute.
a.clue: Think about how much blood is pumped in each single beat.

b.q: Sam trains for 12 weeks by running. Which set of changes would be most likely when he is tested again?
opts: Lower resting heart rate and higher VO₂ max
Lower resting heart rate and lower stroke volume
Higher resting heart rate and higher VO₂ max
Higher resting heart rate and lower stroke volume
b.why: Aerobic training raises stroke volume and VO₂ max, and the larger stroke volume lets resting heart rate fall. The mix of a lower resting heart rate with a lower stroke volume is tempting but reverses the cause: a lower resting rate is the result of a higher stroke volume.
b.clue: Stroke volume and VO₂ max both go up with training.

a.best: Her heart pumps more blood with each beat

b.best: Lower resting heart rate and higher VO₂ max

problems.detail: Why (a) calls the 'pumping less blood each minute' distractor 'the second option', but options are shown in random order (here it is fourth), so the reference can point students to the wrong option. Name the option by its wording instead.

The clue 'Think about how much blood is pumped in each single beat' points straight at the only option about blood per beat, so a student can pick it without understanding the stroke volume and heart rate link.

The clue 'Stroke volume and VO₂ max both go up with training' rules out both lower-stroke-volume options and both lower-VO₂ max options, leaving only the resting heart rate to decide. It gives away most of the answer.

problems.detail: The last bullet puts hypertrophy straight after 'It rises with aerobic training', which implies aerobic training makes muscles grow bigger. Hypertrophy comes mainly from resistance training. Aerobic training mostly improves the muscles' use of oxygen (more mitochondria and capillaries) rather than their size. The card should link hypertrophy to resistance training.
